## Summary

nFore Technology registers five MA-L blocks at Ruiguang Road, Neihu District, Taipei, Taiwan [1]. Its own site describes it as focused on research, development and application of automotive wireless communication technology, offering BT and Wi-Fi modules for short-range in-vehicle links, including the automotive-grade NF3401 BT/Wi-Fi module, alongside C-V2X modules, UWB and Bluetooth smart-key solutions, PLC modules for EV charging, and mmWave and GNSS positioning modules [2].

A MAC in an nFore block is therefore most likely a Bluetooth or Wi-Fi module inside a car head unit, telematics box or smart-key system sold under an automaker's or tier-one supplier's name, not an nFore-branded product, given the company's stated automotive focus [2]. No source in hand documents whether such modules randomise their addresses, so randomization is unknown.

The company site does not state the founding year, headquarters history or customers [2], and the silicon inside its modules and its FCC grantee code were not found: the FCC ID databases refused this session's requests. No security advisory naming nFore was found.
